# Rear bumper bolt removal and torque specs

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Spray bolts with penetrating oil then attach a 1/2-inch drive breaker bar to remove them. [t994]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Spray the bolts with penetrating oil like PB Blaster.
2. Attach a 1/2-inch drive breaker bar and socket to avoid damaging standard ratchets.

_Procedure reported by [t994]._

## Tools

- [Partial] PB Blaster or similar penetrant [t994]
- 1/2-inch drive breaker bar [t994]
- [Partial] Socket [t994]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use leverage by adding a cheater pipe (longer piece of pipe) to the end of the breaker bar. [t994]
- Lie under the truck and kick the breaker bar gently, or place a floor jack under the bar's end for extra force. [t994]
